name: skill_manage

variables.create_where: where a new skill goes (" Global unless where: project."), or empty
variables.files: the supporting-file actions ("write_file / remove_file: supporting files under references/, templates/, scripts/ or assets/."), or empty — the line goes
variables.revert_deleted: " (a deleted one too)" where a deleted skill can be reverted, or empty
variables.index_cut: why the description is kept short (" — only that much shows in the skills list"), or empty

description:
Create, change or delete skills — your procedural memory for kinds of task that come back. Send a list of operations; they apply together, and if one fails none is kept.

- create: a new skill from description + instructions (or content: a whole SKILL.md).{{create_where}}
- patch: fix part of a skill with old_string/new_string (read it with skill_view first) — preferred over rewriting.
- {{files}}
- delete: remove a skill (alone in its call).
- revert: put back the skill as it was before its last change{{revert_deleted}}; the version it replaces is kept, so a second revert undoes the first. Alone in its call.

Write the description as its trigger, in about 60 characters{{index_cut}}: "Use when <situation>. <what it does>." Write lessons, not logs: an instruction and why, no dates or incident stories.

name.description: The skill (lowercase letters, digits, - _ .; up to 64)

description.description: create: when to use the skill, one sentence, the trigger first: "Use when …"

content.description: create, instead of description + instructions: the whole SKILL.md. patch: a whole new SKILL.md — last resort; prefer old_string/new_string.

category.description: create: an optional category directory, e.g. devops

where.description: create: global (every project, the default) or this project's .agent/skills

old_string.description: patch: the exact text to replace (read the skill first)

new_string.description: patch: its replacement; empty deletes it

file_path.description: write_file/remove_file, or patch of a supporting file: a path inside the skill starting with references/, templates/, scripts/ or assets/
